system_description.narrative_title: US-Iran conflict cycle: diplomacy, maritime attacks, and energy risk
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative links shifting US policy and negotiation posture toward Iran (including Trump directives and Vance's role) with a wave of Iranian/IRGC and proxy maritime and regional attacks that threaten shipping and energy infrastructure. Treated as an open system, decisions, retaliatory actions, and international oversight (IAEA) exchange feedbacks with market and security signals; domestic US politics and a changing Congress act as amplifiers and constraints. Maritime incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes create immediate shocks that feed back into diplomacy, military risk calculations, and global energy/security dynamics.
system_description.scope: US executive policy and adviser directives on Iran; JD Vance's negotiation role; Iranian state, IRGC, and proxy (Houthi) military actions; maritime security incidents (tankers, mines, explosions) in the Gulf/Hormuz; IAEA reporting on Iranian enrichment; regional state responses (Saudi, Bahrain, UAE); near‑term market and military risk signals; domestic US political drivers influencing strategy.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical order and energy-security system
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf regional security and proxy warfare (Yemen, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain)
evidence_headlines: Trump says ‘we don’t need a deal with Iran’
JD Vance Emerges as Lead Iran Negotiator
Four tankers struck by explosions in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says
Yemen's Houthis say they attacked pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline
Trump hails ‘positive momentum’ towards ending Iran war

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: Degree and intensity of formal and informal diplomatic contacts and negotiations between the conflict parties and intermediaries.

variables.name: Negotiation posture tone
variables.description: Average conciliatory versus confrontational orientation expressed in negotiation positions and public bargaining statements.

variables.name: Negotiation trust level
variables.description: Mutual confidence that negotiating parties place in each other's commitments and good faith during talks.

variables.name: Military escalation pressure
variables.description: Aggregate force posture, mobilization incentives, and strategic pressures that increase the propensity toward broader military escalation.

variables.name: Kinetic response probability
variables.description: Estimated likelihood that decision-makers will authorize use of kinetic force in response to a provocation within a given timeframe.

variables.name: Proxy operational tempo
variables.description: Rate and intensity of actions carried out by aligned non-state or proxy military actors over time.

variables.name: Maritime incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of hostile incidents, attacks, or hazardous events affecting commercial and military vessels in the maritime theatre.

variables.name: Maritime route risk level
variables.description: Expected hazard level for shipping along key sea lanes based on threat exposure, physical hazards, and navigational constraints.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption risk
variables.description: Probability-weighted expected reduction in energy (fuel/oil/gas) deliveries due to conflict-related interruptions.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: Degree of short-term fluctuations and uncertainty in energy commodity prices driven by security and supply signals.

variables.name: Maritime insurance premium level
variables.description: Market price level for insuring vessels and cargo against regional conflict-related risks and losses.

variables.name: Attribution certainty
variables.description: Confidence in correctly identifying the actor(s) responsible for hostile incidents and attacks.

variables.name: International oversight scrutiny
variables.description: Intensity and visibility of third-party monitoring, reporting, and verification activities regarding contested programs and activities.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: Degree of public opinion, media, and partisan demands exerting influence on policymakers' choices about the conflict.

variables.name: Legislative constraint level
variables.description: Strength of formal and informal legislative limits on executive authority to conduct diplomacy, sanctions, or military action.

variables.name: Intelligence and information flow rate
variables.description: Speed and throughput of actionable intelligence, incident reports, and media information reaching decision-makers and publics.

catalysts.title: Vance-led negotiation push
catalysts.description: Emergence of JD Vance as lead U.S. Iran negotiator driving an active U.S. negotiation initiative and outreach to intermediaries.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'JD Vance Emerges as Lead Iran Negotiator'; 'Vance Considers Direct Talks With Iran Hard-Liner'.

catalysts.title: Potential direct talks between Vance and Iranian hard-liner
catalysts.description: A concrete meeting or direct dialogue between U.S. lead negotiator and an Iranian hard-line interlocutor that could shift diplomatic dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Vance Considers Direct Talks With Iran Hard-Liner' suggests possible imminent direct contact.

catalysts.title: U.S. public restraint stance on strikes
catalysts.description: Public White House signals to advisers to hold off on kinetic strikes absent new provocations, shaping short-term use-of-force decisions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations'.

catalysts.title: Continued mine/explosion incidents in Hormuz
catalysts.description: Ongoing mine/explosion strikes on tankers and vessels in the Strait of Hormuz that raise shipping hazards and attribution disputes.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'Four tankers struck by explosions...'; 'three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz'.

catalysts.title: Houthi proxy attacks and operational uptick
catalysts.description: Repeated Houthi strikes on regional infrastructure and forces increasing proxy activity and regional pressure on policymakers.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Yemen's Houthis say they attacked pumping station'; 'Houthis say they fired missiles at Saudi forces'.

catalysts.title: EU deliberation on labeling Houthis a terrorist group
catalysts.description: Saudi push and EU debate over terrorist designation of Houthis could alter legal/operational constraints and regional responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi Arabia puts pressure on EU to label Yemen's Houthis a terrorist group'.

catalysts.title: New U.S. Congress convenes
catalysts.description: The incoming Congress convening (new composition) may change legislative constraints and oversight affecting the Iran war and diplomacy.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Can a new US Congress mean an end to the Iran war?' implies incoming Congress will alter constraints.

catalysts.title: IAEA intensifies scrutiny of Iranian enrichment
catalysts.description: IAEA concerns and reporting on Iranian enrichment plant drive increased international monitoring and political attention.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says'.

catalysts.title: Possible authorized kinetic response after new maritime/targeted attack
catalysts.description: A new high-profile maritime or radar attack could prompt authorization of kinetic strikes by the U.S. or allies.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: multiple maritime attacks and 'Trump tells advisers he may hold off... barring new provocations'.
